title: Resolver budget non-compliance — impulse.budget=N but resolver allocates >>N
description: Impulse pointer declares budget=1000 (tokens, rows, bytes). Resolver respects metadata.budget on the API surface but the underlying load actually uses 5000. No declared failure_mode — execution succeeds and posterior is updated normally. But the budget metadata that drives downstream planning (binding-layer impulse selection, composition cost estimation) is misleading: future selections based on this 'cheap' impulse will routinely overshoot.

preconditions: task uses an impulse with explicit budget metadata
resolver loads the impulse and reports cost_usd / tokens_used
reported usage is materially higher than the declared budget

impulses.actual_size_hint: Pad memo content to 10000 chars; budget metadata stays at 100 to simulate divergence.

goal_text: Audit resolver executions where the impulse declared a budget but the trace's measured cost (tokens, latency_ms, cost_usd) exceeded the budget by ≥ 2x. Propose a budget-compliance activity that updates impulse metadata to reflect realized cost, and emit a per-resolver compliance scorecard.

detection.signal: Trace's impulse_resolutions[i].cost_usd > 2× the resolved impulse's declared budget (translated to USD via tier-pricing). Pattern is per-resolver, not per-impulse.
detection.query_template: SELECT resolver_id, vessel_id, AVG(cost_usd / declared_budget_usd) as overrun_ratio FROM impulse_resolutions WHERE created_at > time::now() - 7d GROUP BY resolver_id, vessel_id HAVING overrun_ratio > 2.0
